name: yt-04-students
script: Five free A.I. tools for students, and I checked every single limit on the company's own pricing page rather than copying it from a list. One of them is the single best free tool I have found all year. Here is how I check. Roundup articles copy each other, and the numbers rot quietly over months. Nobody goes back and updates them. So I open the pricing page and read what is written on it today. If a limit is not published, I say so instead of guessing. First, Gemini Notebook. You upload your lecture notes or a P.D.F. and it produces an audio overview, which is two voices discussing your own material like a podcast. Revise while you walk. On the free plan you get one hundred notebooks, fifty sources in each one, and three audio overviews per day. Google renamed this from NotebookLM in July. Same product, and the free tier survived the rename intact. Second, SlideSpeak. It turns a document into a presentation, and the important part is that it exports a real PowerPoint file. Most A.I. slide tools trap the result inside their own viewer, so the moment your college wants a P.P.T.X. uploaded you are stuck. This one hands you a genuine file you can keep editing. Free plan is one hundred credits and a fifty megabyte upload cap. Several articles claim it is unlimited. It is not, and their own pricing page says so plainly. Third, Photopea. A full Photoshop class editor that opens in a browser tab with no download and no account. It reads real P.S.D. files with layers intact and exports with no watermark and no daily limit. It runs on your own machine, so your images never get uploaded anywhere. The only catch is ads in a side panel. Fourth, FreeCV. When you start applying for placements, this rewrites your bullet points, writes your summary, and scores your C.V. against the job description before a human ever reads it. No signup, no payment, and the P.D.F. comes out clean with no watermark. Fifth, and this is the best one, Upscayl. It makes old blurry photos sharp, up to sixteen times larger, and it runs entirely on your own computer. It is open source, so no company can ever put it behind a paywall. No account, no credits, no watermark, no cap. Nothing on this list comes close to that. If you only take one thing from this video, take that one. Everything else here has a company behind it that could change its mind. That one cannot.
